newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Empire surges at opening, leads rally.
newsitem.headline: Empire surges at opening, leads rally.

text.p: Empire East Land Holdings Inc surged in early trade, leading A modest rally in the property sector, brokers said.
Empire rose 17.19 percent, or 55 centavos, to 3.75 pesos in early trade amidst heavy turnover. It was the most heavily traded stock at the Philippine Stock Exchange.
Allan Araullo, vice president of Regina Capital Development Corp, said investors were buying up the stock which was battered in recent months due to rumours on its failing financial health.
Empire East was sold down to its all-time low in April due to the persistent rumours despite repeated denials by the company.
Its parent Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc also went up, gaining 7.58 percent to 3.55 pesos.
A trader said a recent report alleging price manipulation in the stock has reinforced the company's position that it was not facing financial difficulties.
Araullo said a foreign brokerage firm had been supporting the issue.
On Tuesday, Empire had risen 40 centavos, or 14.29 percent, to 3.20 pesos.
Other big gainers include Filinvest Land which rose 7.81 percent to 6.90 pesos and Ayala Land Inc which gained 3.49 percent to 22.25 pesos.
The property index rose 34.20 points, or 2.48 percent, to 1,414.32 points.
"The fear of a possible collapse (in the property sector) is no longer there ... But doubts remain," Araullo said.
